tasks.short: Develop watershed protection or rehabilitation plans.

steps.what: Assess actual watershed conditions, existing evidence, constraints and objectives
Choose technically justified watershed protection or rehabilitation measures and monitoring criteria
Write the watershed protection or rehabilitation plan from the selected measures and actual evidence

loop.purpose: Draft a coherent plan from measures selected by the specialist.
loop.input: Actual evidence, constraints, selected measures, rationale and monitoring criteria.
loop.output: Plan draft with source-linked claims and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Specialist checks causal claims, site applicability, intervention intent, uncertainty and monitoring commitments against the actual evidence and decisions.
loop.stop: One draft and correction; missing site facts or unjustified measures return to manual authorship.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native plan headings cannot express site-specific rationale and trade-offs.

steps.what: Check the completed watershed plan v1 against the selected measures, constraints and intended internal planning use
Save the exact checked watershed plan v1 in the same internal project folder

tasks.design: Start with native plan templates in {DOCS}; use a bounded loop only to draft the rationale around the specialist's chosen measures and actual watershed evidence. The specialist retains field assessment, intervention selection and final meaning review before the separate same-folder save; no implementation or permit approval is inferred.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site-specific measures and evidence must be explained coherently rather than just placed in headings.
tasks.enabler_now: A constrained draft can turn explicit specialist decisions into reviewable prose.
tasks.still_hard: Ecological trade-offs, uncertain hydrology and feasibility remain professional decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Choose an intervention appropriate to the actual watershed and its uncertainty.

ambition.what: No added land-use, permit or implementation rights.

tasks.altitude: Less plan prose drafting, with the same watershed assessment and measure-selection duties.

reach.learn: Connect proposed measures to actual ecological evidence and monitoring limits.

evidence.claim: A source-constrained loop can draft plan prose around explicit professional decisions; this is an unmeasured design hypothesis.

assumptions: Boundary is plan development, including its written output. Implementation, consultation decisions and permit submissions receive no saving credit. Shares are provisional, not measured.

The specialist supplies watershed boundary, observation dates, measured conditions, source studies, constraints, selected measures, rationale and monitoring criteria. {OTHER} is the existing water/GIS study repository. Missing site facts are collected or written manually; the model cannot invent a survey or intervention decision.
Test native templates first. No physical study, technical selection or same-system save saving. If the same assessment also feeds a cost-benefit study, allocate the shared investigation once.
research_questions: Does checked drafting preserve site-specific rationale and uncertainty with less rewriting?

already_counted.description: Check generated plan meaning and source fidelity during drafting.

incremental.description: Maintain plan constraints and source permissions as project requirements change.

approvals.approved_version: checked watershed plan v1 for internal planning; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A source-ready plan removes 11.6 of the provisional 29 prose hours, less 1 upkeep. A novel watershed with sparse evidence leaves little reusable prose; assessment, measure decisions, final check and save stay full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write proposals, reports, brochures and other water-resource documents.

steps.what: Choose the document purpose and audience and verify actual water-resource results, project facts and approved commitments
Prepare source tables and figures for wastewater, supply-demand or project reporting using the specified measures
Write the proposal, project report or informational brochure around the checked facts and tables

loop.purpose: Draft water-resource prose for the specified purpose and audience.
loop.input: Checked project facts, argument, tables, sources, uncertainty and approved commitments.
loop.output: Document draft with traceable factual claims.
loop.check: Specialist verifies technical meaning, causal claims, uncertainty, proposal commitments and audience wording against the sources; checks prevent invented benefits and unsupported public advice.
loop.stop: One draft and correction; missing facts or commitments return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native templates and charts cannot explain project results or an approved proposal argument.

steps.what: Check the exact completed water-resource document v1 for technical accuracy, references and authorised use
Save the exact checked water-resource document v1 in the same document store

tasks.design: Configure native {SPREADSHEET} queries and document templates first, producing checked tables from the existing water-data system {OTHER}. Add a bounded {DOCS} prose draft around approved facts and commitments; the specialist checks meaning and the completed version before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Water-resource documents repeat table preparation and source-based explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Refreshable tables and a constrained prose draft can remove repeated assembly without inventing technical claims.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a defensible argument and accepting proposal commitments require the accountable specialist.
tasks.human_edge: Explain water-resource uncertainty and avoid claims the evidence cannot sustain.

ambition.what: No new funding, publication or commitment authority.

tasks.altitude: Less table and first-draft assembly; scientific authorship remains.

reach.learn: Present source-linked evidence and distinguish findings from proposals.

evidence.claim: Native queries and source-grounded prose drafting can support technical documents, with professional checks; no water-specific measured result is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary covers writing the named documents and saving the result, not an assumed grant submission or public website release. If a send or publication exists it must have its own final-version gate. Shares are provisional.

Existing monitoring/project staff produce location, period, measurement, unit, sampling method, quality flag and project facts; the specialist supplies purpose, approved argument, aggregation rules, uncertainty and commitments. Missing values and interpretations are resolved manually before generation. No new monitoring feed is assumed.
Try native queries and templates first. Scientific fact selection, final review and same-system save remain full. Existing system runtime has no labour credit.
unknowns: Actual split among proposals, reports and brochures
Coverage of usable checked source data
research_questions: Which document types show less drafting effort after substantive source checking?

already_counted.description: Check table sources, units and aggregations.
Check generated water-resource prose and commitments.

incremental.description: Maintain query definitions and document constraints as source formats change.

approvals.approved_version: checked water-resource document v1; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A recurring source-ready report removes 7.5 table hours and 22 prose hours per provisional 100 task hours, less 1.5 upkeep. A novel proposal has fewer reusable sources and more original argument; final accuracy review and save remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct cost-benefit studies for watershed improvements or water-management alternatives.

steps.what: Define water-management alternatives, appraisal boundary and justified costs, benefits, time horizon and uncertainty assumptions
Calculate comparable cost-benefit cash flows and specified sensitivity cases for the selected alternatives
Interpret alternative rankings, unpriced effects and sensitivity limits and write the actual cost-benefit study
Check the completed study v1 against appraisal assumptions, calculation outputs and actual decision limitations
Save the exact checked cost-benefit study v1 in the same project folder

tasks.design: Configure a versioned {SPREADSHEET} appraisal workbook for the specialist's chosen alternatives, assumptions and sensitivity cases. Fixed formulas produce comparable cash flows; the specialist checks units and discount timing, interprets unpriced effects and writes the study before its final check and save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable scenario tables can require repeated formulas and manual recalculation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native workbook tables and scenario functions can repeat explicitly specified calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Defensible benefits, ecological trade-offs and uncertainty cannot be selected by a formula.
tasks.human_edge: Identify what the monetary comparison leaves out and whether a ranking is meaningful.

ambition.what: Recheck a specified water-management alternative after a verified cost assumption changes.

tasks.altitude: Less scenario calculation work, without authority to select or fund a project.

reach.learn: Show sensitivity and unpriced ecological effects alongside monetary results.

evidence.claim: Spreadsheet scenario functions can repeat specified cost-benefit arithmetic while appraisal assumptions remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is the appraisal study, not project approval or realised environmental benefit. Shares are provisional.

The specialist supplies alternatives, physical quantities, timing, benefit estimates with provenance, horizon, discount assumptions, uncertainty ranges and treatment of unpriced effects. Finance or suppliers supply source rates with currency and date. Missing quantities or rates require manual evidence gathering, not generated defaults. {OTHER} is the existing watershed study repository.

Try native workbook configuration first. Calculation checks include dimensional consistency, timing and double-counting. No machine runtime or real-world project savings are credited; overlapping baseline research must be allocated once.
unknowns: Current workbook automation and recalculation effort
research_questions: Does a reusable workbook reduce manual scenario work after independent calculation checks?

already_counted.description: Check appraisal calculations, units, timing and sensitivities.
Final study meaning and limitations check.

incremental.description: Maintain workbook formulas and scenario definitions after method changes.

approvals.approved_version: checked cost-benefit study v1; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeatable scenario arithmetic removes 15 of the provisional 30 calculation hours, less 1 upkeep. A largely automated existing workbook has less manual work to remove; assumptions, interpretation, study authorship and save remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Give communities technical help with storm-water monitoring or other water programs.

steps.what: Establish the community's actual storm-water program problem, capabilities and site constraints
Retrieve and check the applicable approved monitoring methods and prior program records for this community
Develop and explain appropriate technical guidance, discuss implementation constraints and check the community's understanding
outputs: actual community advice and agreed limitations

steps.what: Write the actual technical follow-up note and check its final wording, method references, limitations and recipient
inputs: actual community advice and agreed limitations

steps.what: Send the exact checked technical follow-up message v1 to the named community recipient

tasks.design: Configure method tags and community-program links in {DOCS} and the existing water-program register {OTHER}. The specialist still establishes the actual need, judges and explains the technical advice, writes the real follow-up and checks its final version before the separate send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicable monitoring guidance and prior community records can require repeated searches.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata can link current approved methods to program types and sites.
tasks.still_hard: Advice must fit actual local capability, site conditions and uncertainties.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the community's constraints and explain what they can reliably monitor.

ambition.what: No new regulatory or community decision authority.

tasks.altitude: Less reference search before the same personal technical assistance.

reach.learn: State field limitations and capability needs clearly.

evidence.claim: Native method tags and linked records can reduce retrieval for technical assistance.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual conversation, written follow-up and its send. No community fieldwork is transferred or automated. Shares are provisional.

The community provides actual site, program, equipment and capability facts during s1; their participation remains unchanged with no saving credit. Method owners provide approved version, applicability and limits; the specialist manually resolves missing facts and checks currency. No new monitoring feed is assumed.
Test native links first. Advice, written follow-up content, final check and send stay full. If the same note is counted in a separate report task allocate its authorship once.
unknowns: Existing method metadata and search effort
Actual share of assistance requiring written follow-up
research_questions: Can the native library retrieve current methods without hiding their applicability limits?

already_counted.description: Actual written advice, technical meaning and recipient check.

incremental.description: Maintain method applicability links when approved guidance changes.

approvals.approved_version: checked technical follow-up message v1 and exact recipient; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A native reference library removes 6 of the provisional 20 search hours less 1 upkeep. An already linked program has little retrieval saving; all actual consultation, advice writing and send remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less repeated water-resource document and calculation assembly, with professional choices and community support unchanged.
reach: Explain source evidence and uncertainty to natural sciences managers and community partners.
role.ambitious_version: A specialist who can refresh a checked appraisal and prepare a traceable document while retaining watershed decisions and accountability.
